name: TestFlight
author: Enplace
summary: Get an iPhone app's builds onto your own phone with TestFlight, and see each build through.
description: Goes on an app product beside the App Store plugin, and uses its bundle ID and App Store Connect key, so there's nothing to enter twice. It makes a private tester group with you in it that gets every build, with no wait for Apple's review, and shows each build as Apple processes it until it's ready on your phone. Press Send to TestFlight and it asks for a build from whoever the App Store plugin's Builds come from setting picks (Xcode Cloud, an agent on your Mac, or you in Xcode), with the version from Versions and the next build number. It writes each build's What to test from the work done since the last one, and shares the builds with Release cycle.

settings.name: App name
settings.help: The name to give the app in App Store Connect.

settings.name: SKU
settings.help: Your own code for the app in App Store Connect.

settings.name: Language
settings.help: The app's main language, like en-US.

settings.name: Who gets every build
settings.help: The email you sign in to App Store Connect with. Add more with commas; each one must be a user on your App Store Connect team.

settings.name: Tester group
settings.help: The TestFlight group Enplace makes and keeps. It's internal: every build reaches it with no review by Apple.

settings.name: Write What to test
settings.help: Fills in a new build's What to test from the work finished since the build before it, when it's empty.

settings.name: Issuer ID
settings.help: The same key as the App Store plugin's: set it once, there or here. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API.

settings.name: Key ID
settings.help: The ID of the key you generated there. It needs the App Manager or Admin role to look after TestFlight.

settings.name: Private key (.p8)
settings.help: Paste the whole .p8 file, including the BEGIN and END lines.

tools.name: get_testflight
tools.description: An app product's TestFlight: its latest builds (version, build number, state, What to test, when they expire), the tester group and each tester's state, the next build number, and what's left to set up.
